newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Aborigines declare "political war" in Australia.
newsitem.headline: Aborigines declare "political war" in Australia.

text.p: Australia's most powerful Aboriginal leaders on Thursday declared "political war" against Prime Minister John Howard over his government's attempts to wipe out Aboriginal native land title.
Northern Land Council chairman Galarrwuy Yunupingu told an outback meeting of angry Aboriginal leaders that Howard had "made an enemy of the Aboriginal people of this nation".
"I think it is a declaration of war. That means there is going to be a political war between the government and Aboriginal people," Yunupingu told reporters after the meeting.

"This is a revisit to our waterholes to poison it yet again. This is rounding up Aboriginal people into the valleys and a final shootout. This is finally killing off Aboriginal men, women and children one by one."

Native title laws were introduced by the former government three years ago, but became an urgent political issue when the High Court decided last December that land leased to farmers for generations could be liable to Aboriginal claim.
Up to 78 percent of Australia's 7.68 million square kms (2.96 million square miles) could be affected by native title claims.

In an attempt to end a bitter land row between farmers and Aborigines, prime minister Howard has produced a 10-point plan guaranteeing farmers rights to land they have leased since European settlement began more than 200 years ago.
The plan also guarantees Aborigines limited access for traditional purposes, but Aborigines say Howad's plan effectively extinguishes native title.
"Howard must get the message from these people here that his 10-point plan is not acceptable," Yunupingu said.
Over 100 Aboriginal leaders took part at the meeting 600 km (370 miles) southwest of Darwin and a copy of Howard's plan was ceremonially burnt, Australian Associated Press reported.

The leaders, who represent 65,000 Aborigines from northern and central Australia, warned Howard's plan threatened reconciliation between white and black Australia for the benefit of a handful of rich landowners.
Yunupingu said Howard's plan set Aboriginal people's rights back 50 years and they would now have to fight for their future.
Aborigines were only counted as Australian citizens and allowed to vote in 1967. Before that they were governed under flora and fauna laws.
Australia's 300,000 Aborigines are the most disadvantaged group in Australia's 18 million population, with a life expectancy 17 to 20 years less than white Australians.

Historians estimated there may have been as many as 750,000 Aborigines in Australia at the time of white settlement in 1788. Many early settlers regarded Aborigines as pests and tried to eradicate them from their land by shooting them and poisoning their waterholes.
